title.zh: 卷399 列傳一百八十六 吕贤基 邹鸣鹤 戴熙 汤贻汾 张芾 黄琮 陶廷杰 冯培元 孙铭恩 沈炳垣 张锡庚
title.en: Volume 399 Biographies 186: Lv Xianji, Zou Minghe, Dai Xi, Tang Yifen, Zhang Fei, Huang Cong, Tao Tingjie, Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, Zhang Xigeng
title.raw: 卷399 列傳一百八十六 吕贤基 邹鸣鹤 戴熙 汤贻汾 张芾 黄琮 陶廷杰 冯培元 孙铭恩 沈炳垣 张锡庚

sentences.zh: 呂賢基，字鶴田，安徽旌德人。

translations.literal: Lv Xianji, style name Hetian, was a native of Jingde in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Lv Xianji, whose style was Hetian, came from Jingde in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，持正敢言，數論時政得失，多所採用。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary, upheld rectitude and spoke boldly, repeatedly discussing the gains and losses of current policy, and many of his views were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor and then supervising secretary, he was upright and outspoken, repeatedly weighing the strengths and failings of current policy, and much of what he urged was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔上封事，請懋聖學，正人心，育人才，恤民隱，尤被嘉納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, in response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial requesting vigorous imperial learning, rectification of popular sentiment, cultivation of talent, and care for the people's hidden distresses, and this was especially praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's accession, he answered the call for sealed memorials by urging stronger royal study, moral renewal among the people, investment in talent, and attention to popular hardship; the throne especially welcomed his advice.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，超擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted by exception to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was abruptly elevated to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，以時事可危，疏請下詔求言，略曰：「粵西會匪滋事，二年以來，命將出師，尚無成效，甚至圍攻省城，大肆猖獗。

translations.literal: In the second year, because current affairs were perilous, he memorialized requesting an edict calling for advice, stating in summary: 'The secret-society rebels in western Guangdong have risen in disorder; for two years generals have been sent on campaign without success, and the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and run riot on a great scale.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, seeing how grave affairs had become, he memorialized for an edict inviting candid counsel. He wrote in part: 'The Guangxi secret-society rebels have been in revolt for two years. Armies have been dispatched again and again, yet there is still no decisive result; the insurgents have even besieged the provincial capital and grown brazen beyond measure.'

sentences.zh: 南河豐工未能合龍，重運阻滯，災民屯聚，在在堪虞。

translations.literal: The Feng works on the South River have failed to close the breach, grain transport on the Grand Canal is blocked, disaster victims are massed together, and everywhere gives cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng River project on the South River still has not been closed, heavy transport on the Grand Canal is stalled, disaster victims are crowding together, and danger is visible on every side.

sentences.zh: 河工費五百萬，軍需費一千馀萬，部臣束手無措，必致掊克朘削，邦本愈搖。

translations.literal: River works will cost five million, military supplies more than ten million; the ministers of the Board are at their wits' end, which must lead to squeezing and paring away, and the foundation of the state will shake all the more.
translations.idiomatic: River works alone will cost five million taels and military supplies more than ten million; the Board ministers are at a loss, which can only drive ever harsher exactions until the very foundations of the realm tremble.

sentences.zh: 今日事勢，譬之於病，元氣血脈，枯竭已甚，外邪又熾，若再諱疾忌醫，愈難為救。

translations.literal: Today's situation may be compared to illness: vital energy and blood are already severely depleted, while external evils blaze anew; if we again conceal the sickness and shun the physician, rescue will be harder still.
translations.idiomatic: The present situation is like a patient whose vital force is already spent and whose outward malady is raging anew; if the court again hides the illness and refuses the doctor, recovery will only grow harder.

sentences.zh: 惟有開通喉舌，廣覓良方，庶可補救萬一。

translations.literal: Only by opening the throat and tongue and widely seeking good remedies may we hope to remedy the situation even in the slightest degree.
translations.idiomatic: Only by giving voice free rein and gathering remedies from every quarter can we hope to salvage even a fraction of what remains.

sentences.zh: 請特旨令大小臣工悉去忌諱，一改洩沓之故習，各抒所見，以期集思廣益。

translations.literal: He requested a special edict ordering all officials high and low to cast off taboos, thoroughly change the old habit of lax delay, each express his views, and thereby gather many thoughts for broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a special edict requiring every official, high or low, to drop their taboos, break the old habit of foot-dragging, and speak plainly so that many minds might widen the benefit to the state.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，諭部院大臣、九卿、科道有言責者，各據見聞，直言無隱。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the throne instructed the ministers of departments and provinces, the Nine Chief Ministers, and the censorate and supervising secretaries charged with remonstrance each to report according to what they had seen and heard, speaking frankly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial arrived, the throne ordered ministers of departments and provinces, the Nine Chief Ministers, and every censor and supervising secretary with remonstrative duty to speak from what they had witnessed, frankly and without reserve.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，命賢基馳赴安徽會同巡撫蔣文慶及週天爵辦理防剿事宜，賢基疏言：「江寧以東西梁山為要隘，必先扼守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was ordered to hurry to Anhui to join Governor Jiang Wenqing and Zhou Tianjue in handling defense and suppression; Xianji memorialized, saying: 'Jiangning takes the eastern and western Liang Mountains as critical passes, and these must be seized and held first.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he was ordered posthaste to Anhui to work with Governor Jiang Wenqing and Zhou Tianjue on defense and suppression. Xianji memorialized that Jiangning's eastern and western Liang Mountains were the vital passes and had to be held first.

sentences.zh: 廬州為江淮門戶，宜令重臣駐★。

translations.literal: Luzhou is the gateway between the Yangzi and Huai rivers, and a senior minister ought to be stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou was the gateway between the Yangzi and Huai basins, and he urged that a senior minister be stationed there.

sentences.zh: 巢湖出江當梁山上游，地方匪徒宜招撫，免為賊用，且可與梁山為犄角。

translations.literal: Chaohu Lake debouches into the river above the Liang Mountains; local bandits there should be won over by appeasement lest they be used by the rebels, and they could moreover form a pincer with the Liang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Chaohu Lake enters the Yangzi above the Liang Mountains; local bandits there should be pacified so they would not serve the rebels, and they could then support the Liang positions in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納，不及施行，而安慶、江寧先後陷。

translations.literal: The throne praised and accepted this, but before it could be carried out, Anqing and Jiangning fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his plan, but before it could be implemented Anqing and Jiangning had already fallen in turn.

sentences.zh: 奏調給事中袁甲三、知府趙畇幫辦團練防剿，又調編修李鴻章等襄軍事。

translations.literal: He memorialized to transfer Supervising Secretary Yuan Jiasan and Prefect Zhao Yun to assist in organizing militia for defense and suppression, and also transferred Compiler Li Hongzhang and others to aid military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He secured the transfer of Supervising Secretary Yuan Jiasan and Prefect Zhao Yun to help organize militia for defense and suppression, and also brought in Compiler Li Hongzhang and others to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 偕週天爵疏言：「事當分任。

translations.literal: Together with Zhou Tianjue he memorialized, saying: 'Affairs ought to be divided by responsibility.'
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhou Tianjue he submitted a memorial arguing that duties had to be divided clearly.

sentences.zh: 團練專令殲除土匪；

translations.literal: Militia should be charged solely with destroying local bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Militia should be tasked solely with wiping out local bandits;

sentences.zh: 牧令守本境，統帥勦賊，不得遠駐百里之外，以免推諉。

translations.literal: magistrates should guard their own jurisdictions, and commanders suppressing rebels must not station themselves more than a hundred li away, lest they shift blame onto one another.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates should hold their own districts, and field commanders must not camp more than a hundred li away when suppressing rebels, lest each pass the blame to the other.

sentences.zh: 」上韙之。

translations.literal: The throne approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne endorsed their proposal.

sentences.zh: 安徽境內無大枝勁旅，團練亦散漫無可恃。

translations.literal: Within Anhui there were no large branches of crack troops, and the militia too were scattered and not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui had no strong regular contingents on the ground, and the militia were scattered and unreliable.

sentences.zh: 七月，湖北敗賊竄陷英山，擾太湖，分犯洪家埠，賢基檄游擊賡音太、伍登庸擊走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, defeated rebels from Hubei raided into and seized Yingshan, harassed Taihu, and in detachments attacked Hongjiabu; Xianji ordered Brigade Commanders Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month defeated rebels from Hubei swept into Yingshan, harried Taihu, and struck Hongjiabu in separate columns. Xianji ordered Brigade Commanders Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊復自江西竄踞安慶，賢基赴舒城、桐城勸募團練，為官軍聲援。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the rebels again from Jiangxi raided in and seized Anqing; Xianji went to Shucheng and Tongcheng to urge enlistment of militia as a sounding support for the regular army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels again poured in from Jiangxi and seized Anqing. Xianji went to Shucheng and Tongcheng to raise militia and lend the regular forces moral support.

sentences.zh: 賡音太、伍登庸戰歿於集賢關。

translations.literal: Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong died in battle at Jixian Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yintai and Wu Dengyong were killed fighting at Jixian Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊犯桐城，紳士馬三俊率練勇迎戰失利，遂失守。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked Tongcheng; the gentry leader Ma Sanjun led militia to meet them in battle but was defeated, and the city was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels struck Tongcheng, the local gentleman Ma Sanjun led militia into battle and was beaten, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 已革按察使張熙宇退駐大關，賢基抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: The dismissed Provincial Judicial Commissioner Zhang Xiyu had withdrawn and encamped at Daguan; Xianji submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissed Provincial Judicial Commissioner Zhang Xiyu had pulled back to Daguan, and Xianji filed a blunt impeachment memorial against him.

sentences.zh: 時方駐舒城，或告以無守土責，未轄一兵，賊鋒甚銳，可退守以圖再舉。

translations.literal: He was then stationed at Shucheng, and some advised him that he bore no territorial defense duty, commanded not a single soldier, and the rebel spearhead was very sharp, so he could withdraw to defend elsewhere and plan another effort.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was at Shucheng, and some urged that he had no territorial defense duty, commanded no troops of his own, and faced a very sharp rebel thrust, so he ought to fall back and regroup.

sentences.zh: 賢基曰：「奉命治鄉兵殺賊，當以死報國。

translations.literal: Xianji said: 'Ordered to organize local militia and kill rebels, I ought to repay the state with my death.'
translations.idiomatic: Xianji replied: 'I was ordered to organize local militia and kill rebels. I should repay the state with my life.'

sentences.zh: 敢避寇倖免乎？

translations.literal: How dare I evade the bandits and by luck escape?
translations.idiomatic: How could I flee the enemy and hope to survive by chance?

sentences.zh: 」十月賊至，登陴守禦，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebels arrived; he mounted the battlements to defend, the city fell, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels arrived. He mounted the walls to defend the city, and when it fell he died with it.

sentences.zh: 文宗初聞舒城失守，即曰：「賢基素懷忠義，必能大節無虧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong first heard that Shucheng had fallen, he said at once: 'Xianji has long cherished loyalty and righteousness; he is sure to uphold great integrity without stain.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong first heard that Shucheng had fallen, he said at once, 'Xianji has always been loyal and righteous; he is sure to die without dishonor.'

sentences.zh: 」及奏上，深悼惜之，贈尚書銜，加恩於舒城建專祠，擢其子編修錦文以侍讀用，賜銀三千兩，命錦文即日回籍治喪。

translations.literal: When the report came up, he deeply mourned and prized him, posthumously granted the rank of Minister, showed favor by building a special shrine for him at Shucheng, promoted his son Compiler Jinwen to Reader-in-Waiting, bestowed three thousand taels of silver, and ordered Jinwen to return home that very day to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived, the emperor mourned him deeply, granted him posthumous ministerial rank, ordered a special shrine built at Shucheng, promoted his son Compiler Jinwen to Reader-in-Waiting, gave three thousand taels of silver, and commanded Jinwen to return home at once to conduct the funeral.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉世職，祀京師及本籍府城昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and enshrined in the Capital and in the local prefectural Shrine of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: His family received the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and he was enshrined in the capital and in his home prefecture's Shrine of Loyal Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 後安徽請祀鄉賢，特諭：「賢基品行端正，居官忠直，名副其實。

translations.literal: Later Anhui requested his enshrinement among local worthies, and a special edict stated: 'Xianji's conduct was upright in character, and in office he was loyal and straight; the title fits the reality.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Anhui asked that he be honored among local worthies, and a special edict declared, 'Xianji's character was upright and his service loyal and direct; the honor truly fits the man.'

sentences.zh: 」即報可。

translations.literal: This was at once approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was promptly approved.

sentences.zh: 鄒鳴鶴，字鍾泉，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Zou Minghe, style name Zhongquan, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Minghe, whose style was Zhongquan, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，雲南即用知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a magistrate for immediate use in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the second year of Daoguang and received an immediate magistracy in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 親老告近，改發河南，署新鄭，補羅山，有惠政。

translations.literal: Because his parents were aged he petitioned to serve nearer home, was reassigned to Henan, acted as magistrate of Xinzheng, and was confirmed at Luoshan, where he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents grew old he asked to serve closer to home, was reassigned to Henan, served as acting magistrate of Xinzheng and then as magistrate of Luoshan, and won a reputation for humane rule.

sentences.zh: 母喪，去官。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫程祖洛疏陳鳴鶴政績，羅山紳民籥請保留河南，特旨允俟服闋以南、汝、陳、光四府州所屬酌補選缺，異數也。

translations.literal: Governor Cheng Zuluo memorialized Minghe's administrative achievements; the gentry and people of Luoshan jointly petitioned to retain him in Henan, and a special edict allowed that after mourning he might, within the jurisdictions of the four prefectures Nan, Ru, Chen, and Guang, be suitably appointed to selection vacancies—an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Cheng Zuluo reported Minghe's record in office, and Luoshan's gentry and common people petitioned jointly to keep him in Henan. A special edict promised that after his mourning he might be placed in any suitable vacancy within the Nan, Ru, Chen, and Guang prefectures—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 尋補光山，調祥符，擢蘭儀廳河工同知，護開歸陳許道。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was confirmed at Guangshan, transferred to Xiangfu, promoted to Subprefect of River Works in the Lanyi Office, and acted as Intendant of the Kaigui-Chenxu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed at Guangshan, transferred to Xiangfu, promoted to subprefect of river works in the Lanyi Office, and placed in charge of the Kaigui-Chenxu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以治河勞，晉秩知府。

translations.literal: For his labors in river control he was advanced in rank to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His exertions on the rivers earned him promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 歷衛輝、陳州、開封。

translations.literal: He served in succession at Weihui, Chenzhou, and Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Weihui, Chenzhou, and Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，河決祥符，水圍省城，鳴鶴露宿城上，盡力堵禦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the river burst at Xiangfu and the waters besieged the provincial capital; Minghe slept in the open on the city wall and strove with all his strength to block and defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Yellow River broke at Xiangfu and surrounded the provincial capital. Minghe camped on the walls and threw all his strength into holding the flood back.

sentences.zh: 有議遷省城於洛陽者，鳴鶴上議有六不可。

translations.literal: Some proposed moving the provincial capital to Luoyang; Minghe submitted a memorial setting forth six reasons why this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed relocating the provincial capital to Luoyang, but Minghe memorialized six reasons why that could not be done.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣王鼎等據以疏陳，乃決議堅守。

translations.literal: The imperial commissioners Wang Ding and others memorialized on this basis, and the decision was made to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Wang Ding and others took up his argument in their memorial, and the court resolved to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 凡曆七十馀日，水退城安。

translations.literal: In all more than seventy days passed before the waters receded and the city was secure.
translations.idiomatic: After more than seventy days the flood withdrew and the city was safe.

sentences.zh: 論功，晉秩道員。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was advanced in rank to intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，河決中牟，褫職留工，工竣，復原官，仍在工效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the river burst at Zhongmou; he was stripped of office but kept on the works, and when the works were completed his original office was restored while he still served on the project.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the river broke at Zhongmou. He was dismissed from office but kept on the works; when the project was finished his rank was restored and he continued to serve on the river.

sentences.zh: 丁生母憂，服闋，署彰衛懷道，尋授江西督糧道。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his birth mother; when mourning ended he acted as Intendant of the Zhangwei-Huai Circuit, and soon received appointment as Grain Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his birth mother he acted as intendant of the Zhangwei-Huai Circuit and was soon made Jiangxi's grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，詔舉賢才，戶部侍郎侯桐、兩江總督陸建瀛交章以鳴鶴薦，擢順天府尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for worthy talent; Vice Minister of Revenue Hou Tong and Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Lu Jianying each submitted memorials recommending Minghe, and he was promoted to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's accession the throne called for worthy men. Vice Minister Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying both recommended Minghe, and he was made intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was made governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 匪亂方熾，大學士賽尚阿督軍事，鳴鶴課吏治，治團練，撫卹被兵災民。

translations.literal: The rebel turmoil was then blazing; Grand Secretary Sai Shanga supervised military affairs, while Minghe pressed official discipline, organized militia, and comforted the people afflicted by war.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel turmoil was raging, and Grand Secretary Sai Shanga directed military affairs while Minghe tightened administration, organized militia, and relieved those harmed by the fighting.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊由永安突犯桂林，城中兵僅千人，倉猝防禦，提督向榮馳援，民心始定。

translations.literal: In the second year the rebels from Yong'an suddenly attacked Guilin; troops in the city numbered only a thousand, and in haste they defended; Regional Commander Xiang Rong hurried to the rescue, and popular sentiment first settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the rebels burst out of Yong'an and struck Guilin. The city had barely a thousand troops, yet they threw up a hurried defense until Regional Commander Xiang Rong raced to the rescue and the people regained their nerve.

sentences.zh: 總兵秦定三等續至，鳴鶴以諸軍無所統屬，自請督戰。

translations.literal: Brigade Commander Qin Dingsan and others arrived in succession; Minghe, because the various armies had no unified command, requested himself to supervise battle.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Qin Dingsan and others arrived in turn. Seeing that the armies lacked unified command, Minghe volunteered to direct the fighting himself.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將擊賊，相持月馀，賊百計攻城，屢卻。

translations.literal: He dispatched the various generals to strike the rebels; the contest lasted more than a month, and the rebels by every stratagem assaulted the city but were repeatedly repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals out against the rebels. The struggle lasted more than a month; the rebels tried every tactic to take the city and were driven back again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊遂分竄，賽尚阿促向榮追擊，鳴鶴堅留防賊回竄，互疏爭。

translations.literal: The rebels then split and fled in detachments; Sai Shanga urged Xiang Rong to pursue and strike, while Minghe insisted on staying to guard against the rebels' return, and they disputed by mutual memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then broke up and fled in columns. Sai Shanga pressed Xiang Rong to pursue, but Minghe insisted on staying to guard against their return, and the two clashed in opposing memorials.

sentences.zh: 賊尋陷興安、全州，入湖南，詔褫鳴鶴職，以守城功免治罪。

translations.literal: The rebels soon seized Xing'an and Quanzhou and entered Hunan; an edict stripped Minghe of office, but because of his merit in defending the city he was spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon took Xing'an and Quanzhou and pushed into Hunan. Minghe was dismissed from office, but his defense of Guilin spared him further punishment.

sentences.zh: 洎回籍，賊已陷武昌。

translations.literal: By the time he returned to his native place, the rebels had already seized Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned home, the rebels had already taken Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，陸建瀛赴九江督師，疏請起鳴鶴籌辦沿江防務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Lu Jianying went to Jiujiang to supervise the army and memorialized requesting that Minghe be recalled to organize defenses along the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Lu Jianying went to Jiujiang to take command and memorialized to recall Minghe to organize defenses along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 已病，或沮其行。

translations.literal: He was already ill, and some tried to dissuade him from going.
translations.idiomatic: He was already ill, and some urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此吾補過報國之日也！

translations.literal: He said: 'This is the day for me to make amends and repay the state!'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'This is my day to atone and repay the state!'

sentences.zh: 」建瀛旋退江寧，獲罪，命鳴鶴與將軍祥厚等籌商守禦。

translations.literal: Jianying soon withdrew to Jiangning and was punished; Minghe was ordered together with General Xianghou and others to deliberate on defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianying soon fell back to Jiangning and was punished. Minghe was ordered to work with General Xianghou and others on the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 建瀛見其病甚，欲為奏請還家養疴，鳴鶴不可。

translations.literal: Jianying saw how grave his illness was and wished to memorialize requesting that he return home to nurse his sickness, but Minghe would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how ill he was, Lu Jianying wanted to memorialize for permission to send him home to recover, but Minghe refused.

sentences.zh: 及江寧陷，書絕命詞曰：「臣力難圖報稱，臣心仰答九重。

translations.literal: When Jiangning fell he wrote his final words, saying: 'Your servant's strength can hardly achieve repayment; your servant's heart looks up to answer the Ninefold Heights.'
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning fell he wrote his last testament: 'My strength can no longer repay Your Majesty, yet my heart still turns upward to the throne.'

sentences.zh: 三次守城盡節，庶幾全始全終。

translations.literal: Three times defending cities I have exhausted my integrity; may I perhaps complete the beginning and complete the end.
translations.idiomatic: Three times I have held a city to the last; may I now finish as I began.'

sentences.zh: 」遣人持付其子，自率隊出，至三山街，賊見識之，曰：「此守桂林之鄒巡撫也！

translations.literal: He sent someone to deliver it to his son, then himself led a detachment out; at Sanshan Street the rebels recognized him and said: 'This is Governor Zou who defended Guilin!'
translations.idiomatic: He sent the note to his son by messenger, then led a detachment out himself. At Sanshan Street the rebels recognized him and cried, 'This is Governor Zou who held Guilin!'

sentences.zh: 」呼其名詬之。

translations.literal: They called his name and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted his name and cursed him.

sentences.zh: 鳴鶴亦罵不絕口，被支解而死。

translations.literal: Minghe also cursed without cease and was dismembered and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Minghe cursed them without pause until they cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈道銜，賜卹。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted intendant rank and mourning grants were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, he was granted posthumous intendant rank and mourning compensation.

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南既平，曾國籓疏陳鳴鶴生平政績及殉節狀，請加恩優恤。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi, after Jiangnan had been pacified, Zeng Guofan memorialized setting forth Minghe's lifelong administrative achievements and the circumstances of his martyrdom, requesting added favor and generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, after Jiangnan had been pacified, Zeng Guofan memorialized on Minghe's career and martyrdom and asked for added honors and generous condolence.

sentences.zh: 御史硃震言鳴鶴匿民居遇害，非臨陣捐軀者比，請罷之。

translations.literal: Censor Zhu Zhen said that Minghe had hidden in a private dwelling when killed, and was not comparable to one who gave his life on the battlefield, and requested that the honors be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhu Zhen argued that Minghe had been killed while hiding in a private house and was not comparable to a man who died in battle, and asked that the honors be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 編修硃福基等復以鳴鶴被難聞見各殊，呈請下兩江總督馬新貽確查。

translations.literal: Compiler Zhu Fuji and others again noted that accounts of Minghe's death differed, and submitted a request that Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Ma Xinyi conduct a thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Zhu Fuji and others noted that reports of Minghe's death conflicted and asked that Governor-General Ma Xinyi of the Two Jiangs investigate.

sentences.zh: 新貽覆奏紳耆咸稱鳴鶴協同防守，誓以身殉，罵賊被戕，無避匿民居之事。

translations.literal: Xinyi reported back that gentry and elders all said Minghe had joined in the defense, vowed to die with the city, cursed the rebels and was killed, and that there was no matter of hiding in a private dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xinyi reported that local gentry and elders agreed Minghe had helped defend the city, vowed to die with it, cursed the rebels until he was killed, and had not hidden in any private house.

sentences.zh: 詔依巡撫例議卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: An edict ordered condolence according to the precedent for governors, granted the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry together with Commandant of Light Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered condolence on the scale used for governors, granted hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Zhuangjie, 'Steadfast in Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 後祀河南名宦祠。

translations.literal: Later he was enshrined in Henan's Shrine of Eminent Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enshrined in Henan's Shrine of Eminent Officials.

sentences.zh: 戴熙，字醇士，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Dai Xi, style name Chunshi, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xi, whose style was Chunshi, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢贊善，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the great examination he placed in the second class, was promoted to Preceptor, and transferred to Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he placed in the second class, was promoted to preceptor, and then made sub-reader.

sentences.zh: 十八年，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 督廣東學政，任滿，請終養。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Guangdong; when his term ended he requested to care for his parents until their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guangdong education commissioner, and when his term ended he asked leave to care for his parents in their old age.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，服闋，未補官，复督廣東學政，累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended he had not yet received a new appointment when he again supervised education in Guangdong, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, after mourning he had not yet taken a new post when he was again made Guangdong education commissioner and rose step by step to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授兵部侍郎，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of War while still serving in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made Vice Minister of War while continuing in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 先是，廣東因士民阻英人入城，相持者數年。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Guangdong because scholars and common people blocked the English from entering the city, the standoff had lasted several years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guangdong's scholars and common people had blocked the British from entering the city, and the standoff had dragged on for years.

sentences.zh: 至二十九年，英人懾於民怒，暫罷議。

translations.literal: By the twenty-ninth year the English, awed by popular wrath, for the time suspended the negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-ninth year the British, intimidated by popular anger, suspended the talks for the time being.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉悅，以為奇功，錫封總督徐廣縉子爵，巡撫葉名琛男爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong rejoiced and took it for a marvelous achievement, ennobling Governor Xu Guangjin as a baron and Governor Ye Mingchen as a baronet.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was delighted and treated it as a great victory, ennobling Governor Xu Guangjin as a baron and Governor Ye Mingchen as a baronet.

sentences.zh: 會熙召對，論及之。

translations.literal: When Xi was summoned for audience the matter was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was summoned to audience, the matter came up.

sentences.zh: 熙言廣東民風素所諳悉，督撫所奏，恐涉鋪張，非可終恃，上不懌。

translations.literal: Xi said that he was long familiar with Guangdong popular customs, and that what the governor and provincial governor reported probably involved exaggeration and could not be relied on forever; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said he knew Guangdong's popular temper well and feared the governor and provincial governor were exaggerating—nothing to rely on forever. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 尋命書扇，有帖體字，傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to write on a fan and used clerical-style characters; an edict was transmitted rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was told to write on a fan and used clerical-style characters. The throne sent down a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 越日，命南書房書扁額，內監傳諭指派同直張錫庚，戒勿交寫誤字之戴熙。

translations.literal: The next day the Southern Study was ordered to write plaque inscriptions; the eunuchs transmitted instructions assigning his colleague on duty Zhang Xigeng and warning them not to give the work to Dai Xi, who wrote mistaken characters.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Southern Study was ordered to write plaque inscriptions. The eunuchs directed that his colleague Zhang Xigeng do the work and warned them not to entrust it to Dai Xi, who had written erroneous characters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷其入直。

translations.literal: Before long his service in the Southern Study was ended.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed from the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 熙知眷衰，稱病請開缺，上益怒，降三品京堂休致。

translations.literal: Xi knew imperial favor was waning, pleaded illness and requested to vacate his post; the emperor grew still angrier and demoted him to third-rank Beijing official with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing imperial favor fade, Xi pleaded illness and asked to leave office. The emperor grew angrier still and retired him as a third-rank Beijing official.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，詔舉人才，尚書孫瑞珍以熙薦，召來京候簡用，因病未至。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng an edict called for talent; Minister Sun Ruizhen recommended Xi, and he was summoned to the capital to await selection, but because of illness did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng the throne called for talent. Minister Sun Ruizhen recommended Xi, and he was summoned to the capital to await appointment, but illness kept him away.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞江寧，浙江戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebels occupied Jiangning, and Zhejiang was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Jiangning, and Zhejiang went on alert.

sentences.zh: 熙偕官紳勸諭捐輸，舉行團練。

translations.literal: Xi together with officials and gentry urged contributions and organized militia.
translations.idiomatic: Xi worked with officials and gentry to urge donations and organize militia.

sentences.zh: 八年，粵匪由江西擾浙東，熙助巡撫晏端書籌調兵食，乞援鄰境。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Guangdong rebels from Jiangxi harassed eastern Zhejiang; Xi assisted Governor Yan Duanshu in planning deployment of troops and provisions and begged aid from neighboring jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year rebels from Jiangxi harried eastern Zhejiang. Xi helped Governor Yan Duanshu arrange troops and supplies and seek aid from neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 援師至，賊未得逞，漸退。

translations.literal: Relief troops arrived, the rebels could not succeed, and gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces arrived, the rebels failed to break through, and gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以治團練勞，加二品頂戴。

translations.literal: For his labors in organizing militia he was granted the second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: For his work organizing militia he was granted second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 杭州初有民兵八百人，又選鋒數百，事緩，以資絀，減少半。

translations.literal: Hangzhou at first had eight hundred militia, and several hundred more were selected as shock troops; when affairs eased they were kept as a reserve force and reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou first raised eight hundred militia and several hundred picked shock troops; when the crisis eased they were kept in reserve and the force was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵匪由安徽廣德入浙，連陷數縣，犯湖州、武康。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Guangdong rebels from Guangde in Anhui entered Zhejiang, seized several counties in succession, and attacked Huzhou and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year rebels from Guangde in Anhui poured into Zhejiang, took several counties in succession, and threatened Huzhou and Wukang.

sentences.zh: 熙以所部練勇付按察使段光清，會旗兵防獨松、千秋等關。

translations.literal: Xi placed the militia under his command in the hands of Provincial Judicial Commissioner Duan Guangqing, and together with banner troops defended the passes at Dusong, Qianqiu, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Xi handed his militia to Provincial Judicial Commissioner Duan Guangqing and joined banner troops in defending Dusong, Qianqiu, and other passes.

sentences.zh: 賊至，斂兵入城守。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, the troops were drawn in to defend within the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the troops were pulled back inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 熙謂用兵無獨守孤城之理，宜分營城外相犄角，又議乘賊初至迎擊，皆未行。

translations.literal: Xi said that in employing troops there was no principle of defending a lone city by itself; camps ought to be divided outside the walls in mutual support, and he also proposed striking the rebels as they first arrived, but none of this was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued that armies should not defend a lone city in isolation, that camps ought to be posted outside the walls in mutual support, and that the rebels should be met as they arrived; none of it was done.

sentences.zh: 熙與弟燾助守西北隅，砲斃黃衣賊一人，賊遽退匿山後。

translations.literal: Xi and his younger brother Tao helped defend the northwest corner; cannon fire killed one rebel in yellow garments, and the rebels abruptly withdrew and hid behind the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his younger brother Tao helped hold the northwest corner. Cannon fire killed a rebel in yellow, and the enemy abruptly fell back behind the hills.

sentences.zh: 眾謂賊且遁，熙料其詐，偵之，果轉赴西南。

translations.literal: The crowd said the rebels were about to flee; Xi judged it a ruse, sent scouts, and they indeed turned toward the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Others thought the rebels were retreating, but Xi suspected a ruse, sent scouts, and found them turning toward the southwest.

sentences.zh: 晝夜環攻，久雨，兵疲。

translations.literal: Day and night they besieged the city on all sides; the rains were prolonged and the troops grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged the city day and night. Endless rain exhausted the defenders.

sentences.zh: 賊於宋鎮湖門故址穴地轟城，遂陷，熙赴水死之。

translations.literal: The rebels at the old site of Songzhen's Humen Gate tunneled underground and blasted the wall; the city fell, and Xi threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tunneled under the old Humen Gate site and blasted the wall. The city fell, and Xi drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 弟煦、媳金、及甥王朝榮，同殉。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu, his daughter-in-law Jin, and his nephew Wang Chaorong died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu, his daughter-in-law Jin, and his nephew Wang Chaorong died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈尚書銜，建專祠，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted ministerial rank, a special shrine was built, he received the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, and was given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, he was granted posthumous ministerial rank, a special shrine was built, his family received hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Refined Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 弟煦，精算學，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was expert in mathematics and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu, a master of mathematics, has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 熙雅尚絕俗，尤善畫。

translations.literal: Xi cultivated refinement beyond the common run and was especially skilled at painting.
translations.idiomatic: Xi cultivated an aloof refinement and was especially gifted at painting.

sentences.zh: 當視學廣東，陛辭，宣宗諭曰：「古人之作畫，須行萬里路。

translations.literal: When he was to supervise studies in Guangdong and took leave at court, Emperor Xuanzong instructed him, saying: 'The ancients in making paintings had to travel ten thousand li.'
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave at court before going to Guangdong as education commissioner, Emperor Xuanzong told him, 'The ancients said a painter must travel ten thousand li.'

sentences.zh: 此行遍歷山川，畫當益進。

translations.literal: On this journey you will traverse mountains and rivers; your painting ought to advance all the more.
translations.idiomatic: On this journey you will see mountains and rivers everywhere; your painting should improve all the more.'

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus highly was he regarded.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後以直言黜。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for speaking too bluntly.

sentences.zh: 及殉節，遂益為世重。

translations.literal: When he died for his integrity, he came to be valued all the more by the world.
translations.idiomatic: After he died for his integrity, the world valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 同時湯貽汾畫負盛名，與熙相匹。

translations.literal: At the same time Tang Yifen enjoyed great fame in painting and was a match for Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Tang Yifen enjoyed great fame as a painter and was Xi’s equal.

sentences.zh: 亦殉江寧之難，同以忠義顯，世稱戴、湯雲。

translations.literal: He too died in the Jiangning calamity; both became renowned for loyalty and righteousness, and the age called them Dai and Tang together.
translations.idiomatic: He too died in the fall of Jiangning. Both became famous for loyalty and righteousness, and the age spoke of them together as Dai and Tang.

sentences.zh: 貽汾，字雨生，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Yifen, style name Yusheng, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yifen, whose style was Yusheng, came from Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 祖大奎，官福建鳳山知縣，守城殉節，父荀業同死，見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dakui served as magistrate of Fengshan in Fujian, died defending the city in martyrdom, and his father Xunye died with him; see the Loyal Martyrs biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dakui had been magistrate of Fengshan in Fujian and died defending the city; his father Xunye died with him. Their story appears in the Loyal Martyrs biographies.

sentences.zh: 貽汾少有俊才。

translations.literal: Yifen in youth had outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yifen showed outstanding talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 家貧，以難廕襲世職，授守備，累擢浙江樂清協副將。

translations.literal: His family was poor; because of the hardship grant he inherited a hereditary office, was appointed garrison commander, and was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Brigade Commander of the Yueqing Garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. He inherited a hereditary office through the hardship grant, became a garrison commander, and rose step by step to deputy brigade commander of the Yueqing garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歷官治軍捕盜有聲。

translations.literal: In successive offices he won renown for governing troops and capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts he won renown for drilling troops and capturing bandits.

sentences.zh: 尚氣節，工詩畫，政績文章為時重。

translations.literal: He prized integrity, was skilled in poetry and painting, and his administrative achievements and writings were valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity, excelled in poetry and painting, and his service and writings were widely respected.

sentences.zh: 晚辭官僑居江寧。

translations.literal: In his later years he resigned office and lived as a sojourner in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he resigned and lived in Jiangning as a retired gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及粵匪熾，貽汾見時事日亟，語人曰：「吾年七十有七，家世忠孝。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong rebels blazed up, Yifen saw daily affairs growing urgent and said to others: 'I am seventy-seven years old, and my family for generations has been loyal and filial.'
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion flared, Yifen saw affairs growing desperate and told others, 'I am seventy-seven, and my family has been loyal for generations.'

sentences.zh: 脫有不幸，惟當致命遂志，以見先人。

translations.literal: If misfortune should come, I can only consign my life to fulfill my resolve and thereby show myself to my forebears.
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune comes, I can only give my life to fulfill my duty and show myself worthy of my forebears.'

sentences.zh: 」江寧籌防，大吏每有諮詢，盡言贊畫。

translations.literal: In planning Jiangning's defenses, the high officials often consulted him, and he spoke fully in support of their plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning prepared its defenses, senior officials often sought his advice, and he gave them his full counsel.

sentences.zh: 城陷，從容賦絕命詞，赴水死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he calmly composed his final words and went into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he calmly wrote his last testament and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗以其三世死事，特詔優恤，加一云騎尉，諡貞愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Wenzong because three generations of his family had died in service issued a special edict for generous condolence, added one Commandant of Light Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong, honoring three generations of death in service, ordered especially generous condolence, added one Commandant of Light Cavalry to the family grant, and gave him the posthumous title Zhenmin, 'Steadfast and Compassionate.'

sentences.zh: 張芾，字小浦，陝西涇陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei, style name Xiaopu, was a native of Jingyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei, whose style was Xiaopu, came from Jingyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷庶子，直南書房。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Sub-Preceptor and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the sub-preceptor ranks and entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 大考一等，擢少詹事，超遷內閣學士，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the great examination he placed in the first class, was promoted to Junior Mentor, was promoted by exception to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he placed in the first class, became junior mentor, was abruptly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and served as Jiangsu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授工部侍郎，任滿回京，仍直南書房，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works; when his term ended he returned to the capital, still served in the Southern Study, and was transferred to the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was made Vice Minister of Works. When his term ended he returned to the capital, remained in the Southern Study, and was transferred to the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，督江西學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he supervised education in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he became Jiangxi education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，請明黜陟，寬出納，禁糜費，重海防，上嘉納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, in response to an edict he presented counsel requesting clear promotion and demotion, lenient receipts and disbursements, prohibition of wasteful expenditure, and emphasis on coastal defense; the emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's accession he answered the call for memorials by urging clear promotion and demotion, easier revenue handling, an end to waste, and stronger coastal defense; the throne welcomed his advice.

sentences.zh: 命按巡撫陳阡被劾各款，得實，罷之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate the various charges impeaching Governor Chen Qian; they were found true and Chen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to investigate the charges against Governor Chen Qian, found them substantiated, and Chen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 阡亦訐芾收受陋規，詔免議。

translations.literal: Qian also denounced Fei for receiving petty customary fees; an edict ordered that this not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Chen also accused Fei of taking petty customary fees, but an edict ordered the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 任滿，留署江西巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was retained to act as Governor of Jiangxi, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was kept on as acting governor of Jiangxi and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪方圍長沙，詔芾偕在籍尚書陳孚恩籌防。

translations.literal: At the time the Guangdong rebels were besieging Changsha; an edict ordered Fei together with the retired Minister Chen Fu'en to plan defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were then besieging Changsha, and Fei was ordered to work with the retired minister Chen Fu'en on defenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，岳州陷，芾駐守九江。

translations.literal: Before long Yuezhou fell, and Fei stationed himself to defend Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuezhou fell, and Fei took post at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，總督陸建瀛至九江，芾移守瑞昌，賊來犯，擊走之，而九江遂陷，革職留任，退守南昌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Governor-General Lu Jianying reached Jiujiang; Fei shifted to defend Ruichang, the rebels came to attack and were beaten off, but Jiujiang then fell; he was stripped of office but kept on duty, and withdrew to defend Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Governor-General Lu Jianying reached Jiujiang. Fei moved to Ruichang, beat back a rebel attack, but Jiujiang then fell. He was dismissed yet kept on duty and fell back to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 賊既踞江寧，分股溯江而上。

translations.literal: Once the rebels held Jiangning, detachments moved up the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels seized Jiangning, columns pushed up the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 芾奏調湖北按察使江忠源來援，甫至而賊船直抵城下，芾率官紳嬰城固守，賊穴道轟城，壞而復完。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized to transfer Hubei Provincial Judicial Commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan to come to the rescue; he had just arrived when rebel boats reached directly beneath the walls; Fei led officials and gentry to bind themselves to the city in stubborn defense; the rebels tunneled and blasted the wall, which was broken and then repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Fei memorialized for Jiang Zhongyuan, Hubei's provincial judicial commissioner, to reinforce him. Jiang had barely arrived when rebel boats reached the walls. Fei led officials and gentry in a desperate defense. The rebels tunneled under the wall and blasted a breach, but it was repaired.

sentences.zh: 總兵馬濟美戰歿城外，賴江忠源迭戰卻賊，被圍凡三閱月，賊乃東走，由九江趨安徽。

translations.literal: Brigade Commander Ma Jimei died fighting outside the walls; relying on Jiang Zhongyuan, who fought repeatedly and repelled the rebels, they were besieged for three months in all before the rebels went east, from Jiujiang toward Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Ma Jimei was killed outside the walls. Jiang Zhongyuan fought them back again and again through a siege of three months before the rebels withdrew east from Jiujiang toward Anhui.

sentences.zh: 芾以守城勞，復原官。

translations.literal: Fei because of his labors in defending the city was restored to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was restored to office for his defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 奏將將吏猥多，部議覈減，芾疏爭，嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: He memorialized that generals and officers were excessively numerous; the Board proposed verification and reduction; Fei memorialized in protest, and a stern edict sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that too many officers had been rewarded. The Board proposed cuts. Fei protested in a memorial and received a sharp imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 會因截留滇、黔銅鉛銀，又陳孚恩被劾，芾為申辨，上怒，褫芾職。

translations.literal: At the same time, because he had intercepted Yunnan and Guizhou copper, lead, and silver, and because Chen Fu'en was impeached and Fei spoke in his defense, the emperor was angry and stripped Fei of office.
translations.idiomatic: He had also intercepted Yunnan and Guizhou copper, lead, and silver shipments, and when Chen Fu'en was impeached he spoke in Chen's defense. The emperor was angry and dismissed Fei.

sentences.zh: 芾既罷，道梗不得歸，僑居紹興。

translations.literal: After Fei was dismissed, the routes were blocked and he could not return home, so he lived as a sojourner in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal the roads were blocked and he could not return home, so he stayed in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 賊窺徽、寧急，巡撫駐廬州不能兼顧。

translations.literal: The rebels watched Huizhou and Ningguo in distress, while the governor was stationed at Luzhou and could not attend to both.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threatened Huizhou and Ningguo while the governor was at Luzhou and could not cover both fronts.

sentences.zh: 侍郎王茂廕薦芾，乃命交和春、福濟差遣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Maoyin recommended Fei, and he was ordered placed at the disposal of He Chun and Fu Ji for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Maoyin recommended Fei, and he was placed under He Chun and Fu Ji for assignment.

sentences.zh: 芾至，練團勸捐，以千人守徽州，提督鄧紹良、總兵江長貴分扼要隘。

translations.literal: When Fei arrived he organized militia and urged contributions, kept a thousand men to defend Huizhou, and Regional Commander Deng Shaoliang and Brigade Commander Jiang Changgui held key passes separately.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei arrived he organized militia and urged donations, kept a thousand men in Huizhou, and placed Regional Commander Deng Shaoliang and Brigade Commander Jiang Changgui at key passes.

sentences.zh: 五年，复休寧、石埭，予六品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he recovered Xiuning and Shidi and was granted sixth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he recovered Xiuning and Shidi and was granted sixth-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊擾婺源、祁門，連破之於七里橋、屯溪口，徽境得安，加五品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the rebels harassed Wuyuan and Qimen; he defeated them in succession at Qili Bridge and Tunkou, Huizhou territory was secured, and he was granted fifth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year rebels harassed Wuyuan and Qimen. He defeated them at Qili Bridge and Tunkou, secured Huizhou, and received fifth-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊復由江西竄踞休寧，擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels again from Jiangxi raided in and seized Xiuning; he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: That winter rebels again poured in from Jiangxi and seized Xiuning; he drove them out.

sentences.zh: 母喪，奪情留軍，命俟服闋後以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he was retained in service despite mourning, and ordered that after mourning ended he might await appointment as third-rank Beijing official.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was kept on duty despite mourning and promised appointment as a third-rank Beijing official after mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 七年，鄧紹良戰歿灣沚，祁門、婺源皆告急。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Deng Shaoliang died fighting at Wanzhi; Qimen and Wuyuan both reported emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Deng Shaoliang was killed at Wanzhi, and Qimen and Wuyuan both sent urgent appeals.

sentences.zh: 遣參將王慶麟破賊於清華街，又擊走祁門賊。

translations.literal: He dispatched Colonel Wang Qinglin to defeat the rebels at Qinghua Street and again to drive off the Qimen rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Colonel Wang Qinglin to defeat the rebels at Qinghua Street and then to drive them out of Qimen.

sentences.zh: 九年，复婺源，賊西竄，授芾通政使，尋遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he recovered Wuyuan; the rebels fled west; Fei was appointed Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Studs, and soon transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he recovered Wuyuan and the rebels fled west. Fei was made commissioner of the Court of Imperial Studs and soon promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太平、石埭連戰皆捷，詔皖南四府一州軍務歸芾督辦。

translations.literal: At Taiping and Shidi successive battles were all victorious; an edict placed military affairs of the four prefectures and one department of southern Anhui under Fei's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: He won successive victories at Taiping and Shidi, and an edict placed military affairs in the four prefectures and one department of southern Anhui under his supervision.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊复陷涇縣、旌德，由績溪進犯徽郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the rebels again seized Jingxian and Jingde and advanced through Jixi to attack Huizhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the rebels again took Jingxian and Jingde and advanced through Jixi against Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 芾督江長貴及知府蘇式敬、道員蕭翰慶，連克太平、旌德、石埭、涇縣，而賊由江蘇、浙江回竄，复連陷建平、廣德、涇縣。

translations.literal: Fei supervised Jiang Changgui together with Prefect Su Shijing and Intendant Xiao Hanqing, and in succession recovered Taiping, Jingde, Shidi, and Jingxian; but the rebels from Jiangsu and Zhejiang returned in raids and again seized Jianping, Guangde, and Jingxian in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fei directed Jiang Changgui, Prefect Su Shijing, and Intendant Xiao Hanqing in recovering Taiping, Jingde, Shidi, and Jingxian in turn. Then rebels returning from Jiangsu and Zhejiang seized Jianping, Guangde, and Jingxian again.

sentences.zh: 芾先以失機自劾，暫行革職留軍，至是復自請治罪，遂命以皖南軍事畀兩江總督曾國籓，召芾還京，請回籍補持服，允之。

translations.literal: Fei had earlier impeached himself for missing his opportunity and was temporarily stripped of office but kept with the army; now he again requested punishment; he was then ordered to hand southern Anhui military affairs to Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Zeng Guofan, summoned back to the capital, and requested to return home to complete mourning, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had already impeached himself for a missed opportunity and been dismissed yet kept with the army. He now asked to be punished again. Southern Anhui was transferred to Governor-General Zeng Guofan, Fei was recalled to the capital, and his request to return home to complete mourning was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪、捻匪合擾關中，起芾助治團練禦賊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Guangdong rebels and Nian bandits together harassed Guanzhong; Fei was recalled to assist in organizing militia to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year rebels and Nian bandits together harassed Guanzhong, and Fei was recalled to help organize militia.

sentences.zh: 事甫平，而回匪亂作，連破數州縣，逼省城，詔芾督辦陝西團練，會同巡撫瑛棨防剿。

translations.literal: Affairs had just settled when the Hui rebel turmoil broke out, several prefectures and counties were taken in succession, and the provincial capital was pressed; an edict ordered Fei to supervise Shaanxi militia organization and join Governor Yingqi in defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Matters had barely settled when Hui rebels rose, took several counties in succession, and threatened the provincial capital. Fei was ordered to supervise Shaanxi militia and work with Governor Yingqi on defense.

sentences.zh: 瑛棨巽懦，計無所出，謂芾大臣有鄉望，諭之宜可解。

translations.literal: Yingqi was compliant and timid, with no plan to offer, and said that Fei as a great minister had prestige in his home region and instructed him that he ought to be able to resolve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi was timid and had no plan. He said Fei, as a senior minister with prestige in the region, ought to be able to settle the matter and urged him to try.

sentences.zh: 芾慨然率數騎往，歷高陵、臨潼至渭南倉頭鎮，曉以利害，回眾頗感動。

translations.literal: Fei resolutely led several horsemen thither, passing Gaoling and Lintong to Cangtou Town in Weinan, and explained the gains and losses; the Hui crowd was considerably moved.
translations.idiomatic: Fei resolutely rode out with a few horsemen through Gaoling and Lintong to Cangtou in Weinan and explained the stakes to the rebels. Many were moved.

sentences.zh: 其酋任老五懼搖眾心，嗾黨擁出折辱之，芾據地大罵不絕口，遂被支解。

translations.literal: Their chief Ren Laowu feared that popular sentiment would be shaken, incited his followers to rush out and humiliate him; Fei sat on the ground and cursed without cease, and was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader Ren Laowu feared the crowd would waver and incited his men to rush out and humiliate him. Fei sat on the ground and cursed without pause until they cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 時同治元年五月十三日也。

translations.literal: This was on the thirteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the thirteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子師劬，往覓遺骸，僅得骨數節。

translations.literal: His son Shijiao went to search for the remains and recovered only a few sections of bone.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shijiao went to recover the body and found only a few fragments of bone.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡文毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, his family received hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous title Wenyi, 'Cultivated Resolve.'

sentences.zh: 命於省城、倉頭鎮並建專祠，隨行遇害之臨潼知縣繆樹本、山西知縣蔣若訥及家屬在涇陽被害者五十二人，從死僕人金榜等六人，並附祀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to have special shrines built at the provincial capital and Cangtou Town; Lintong Magistrate Miao Shuben, Shanxi Magistrate Jiang Ruone, and others killed on the journey, fifty-two family members killed at Jingyang, and six servants who died with him such as Jin Bang, were all enshrined together.
translations.idiomatic: Special shrines were ordered at the provincial capital and Cangtou. Magistrate Miao Shuben of Lintong, Magistrate Jiang Ruone of Shanxi, fifty-two family members killed at Jingyang, and six servants including Jin Bang who died with him were all enshrined there as well.

sentences.zh: 賜師劬舉人。

translations.literal: Shijiao was granted the rank of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao was granted the rank of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 江西、徽州並建專祠，後祀江西名宦。

translations.literal: Special shrines were also built in Jiangxi and Huizhou; later he was enshrined in Jiangxi's Shrine of Eminent Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Special shrines were also built in Jiangxi and Huizhou, and he was later honored in Jiangxi's Shrine of Eminent Officials.

sentences.zh: 黃琮，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Huang Cong was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 道光六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 累擢兵部侍郎，以親老乞養回籍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War, and because his parents were aged petitioned to retire and care for them, returning to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of War, then asked leave to care for his aged parents and returned home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，雲南迴亂方熾，命琮偕在籍御史竇垿治團練。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the Yunnan Hui rebellion was blazing; Cong was ordered together with the retired Censor Dou Qi to organize militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the Yunnan Hui rebellion was raging, and Cong was ordered to organize militia with the retired censor Dou Qi.

sentences.zh: 時餉絀兵單，疆臣主且剿且撫，而漢、回仇隙素深，團練驕悍不聽約束，往往撫局將成，練勇擅殺降回，益紛擾。

translations.literal: At the time funds were short and troops few; frontier officials favored both suppressing and appeasing, but Han and Hui enmity ran deep, militia were arrogant and fierce and would not obey restraint, and often just as pacification was about to succeed the militia on their own killed surrendered Hui, increasing disorder all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were short and troops few. Frontier officials favored both fighting and negotiating, but Han-Hui hatred ran deep. Militia were arrogant and unruly, and just as peace talks neared success they often killed surrendered Hui on their own, making matters worse.

sentences.zh: 總督吳振棫劾琮及竇垿辦理失當，皆褫職。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Zhenbang impeached Cong and Dou Qi for improper handling, and both were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Zhenbang impeached Cong and Dou Qi for mishandling affairs, and both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，振棫疏陳縱容練勇諸事，皆出竇垿主持。

translations.literal: When affairs had settled somewhat, Zhenbang memorialized that the indulgence of the militia and related matters had all been directed by Dou Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs had settled somewhat, Wu reported that indulgence of the militia had all been Dou Qi's doing.

sentences.zh: 琮當省城被圍時，登陴固守有勞，又勸捐出力，詔復原官。

translations.literal: When the provincial capital was besieged, Cong mounted the battlements to defend steadfastly with merit, and also urged contributions with exertion; an edict restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial capital was besieged, Cong helped hold the walls and urged donations. An edict restored his office.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，逆回馬榮詐降，入城戕總督潘鐸，肆殺掠，琮遇害，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, ran riot in slaughter and plunder, and Cong was killed; he was posthumously granted Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city, killed Governor Pan Duo, and slaughtered and plundered the populace. Cong was killed and granted posthumous rank as right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，巡撫潘鼎新為請，予諡文潔。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, Governor Pan Dingxin requested on his behalf and he was given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign Governor Pan Dingxin secured for him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Refined Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 陶廷傑，貴州都勻人。

translations.literal: Tao Tingjie was a native of Duyun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Tingjie came from Duyun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，由編修遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, and from compiler was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, rose from compiler to censor, and then became supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光中，出為江蘇蘇松糧儲道。

translations.literal: During Daoguang he went out to serve as Grain Storage Commissioner of Susong in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he became grain storage commissioner of Susong in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 歷甘肅按察使、陝西布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Provincial Judicial Commissioner of Gansu and Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi, and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gansu's provincial judicial commissioner and Shaanxi's provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，貴州土匪起，命廷傑在籍會同地方官辦理團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng bandits rose in Guizhou; Tingjie was ordered while at home to join local officials in organizing militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng Guizhou bandits rose, and Tingjie was ordered to organize militia at home with local officials.

sentences.zh: 六年，古州、黃平、都勻先後陷，廷傑率團練禦賊，死之，予騎都尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Guzhou, Huangping, and Duyun fell in succession; Tingjie led militia to resist the rebels and died; he was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry and given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Guzhou, Huangping, and Duyun fell in turn. Tingjie led militia against the rebels and was killed. His family received the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 馮培元，字因伯，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Feng Peiyuan, style name Yinbo, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Peiyuan, whose style was Yinbo, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年一甲三名進士，授編修，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he placed third among the first class of jinshi graduates, was appointed compiler, and entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he placed third in the first class of jinshi graduates, became a compiler, and entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，改直上書房，授惇郡王奕脤讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to the Upper Study and instructed Prince Dun Yi Suo in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was moved to the Upper Study to tutor Prince Dun, Yi Suo.

sentences.zh: 二年，大考二等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the second year, in the great examination he placed in the second class and was promoted to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he placed in the second class in the palace examination and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 尋督湖北學政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he supervised education in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hubei education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數月中，連擢侍講學士、光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Within several months he was promoted in succession to Reader of the Hanlin Academy and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted in turn to Hanlin reader and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪已犯長沙，人情洶懼。

translations.literal: At the time the Guangdong rebels had already attacked Changsha, and popular sentiment was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already struck Changsha, and fear ran through the province.

sentences.zh: 培元幼孤，家貧，母何賢明苦節，撫之成立。

translations.literal: Peiyuan was orphaned young and his family was poor; his mother He was worthy and wise and upheld bitter integrity, rearing him until he was established.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyuan lost his father young and grew up poor. His mother He was wise and steadfast, and raised him to manhood.

sentences.zh: 及至湖北，將迎養。

translations.literal: When he reached Hubei he was about to bring her to live with him in support.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hubei he planned to bring her to live with him.

sentences.zh: 聞岳州陷，馳書止母行。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yuezhou had fallen, he sent a hurried letter stopping his mother from traveling.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Yuezhou had fallen, he wrote urgently telling her not to come.

sentences.zh: 母報曰：「如果有變，見危授命，大節不可奪。

translations.literal: His mother replied, saying: 'If there should be change, when danger appears consign your life; great integrity cannot be wrested away.'
translations.idiomatic: His mother replied, 'If trouble comes, give your life when danger appears. Great integrity must not be lost.'

sentences.zh: 其遵吾教！

translations.literal: Obey my teaching!'
translations.idiomatic: Do as I have taught you!'

sentences.zh: 」培元奉書，涕泣自矢。

translations.literal: Peiyuan received the letter and with tears vowed himself to it.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyuan received the letter, wept, and vowed to obey.

sentences.zh: 賊至攻城，培元偕在城文武登陴同守。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived and assaulted the city, Peiyuan together with the civil and military officials in the city mounted the battlements to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked the city, Peiyuan joined the civil and military officials on the walls.

sentences.zh: 城陷，投井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，賊去，向榮率兵入城，有以告者，始出而殮之，屍如生。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the rebels departed; Xiang Rong led troops into the city; when someone reported it, they at last drew him out and encoffined him, and his corpse was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the rebels withdrew. Xiang Rong entered the city, and when someone reported what had happened, Peiyuan was taken from the well and buried; his body looked as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗以武昌之陷，闔城文武殉難，卹典特優，贈侍郎，建專祠，予騎都尉世職，諡文介。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Wenzong because of the fall of Wuchang and the martyrdom of all civil and military officials in the city granted especially generous condolence, posthumously made him Vice Minister, built a special shrine, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong, honoring the fall of Wuchang and the martyrdom of the city's officials, ordered especially generous condolence, granted him posthumous vice-ministerial rank, built a special shrine, gave his family the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and bestowed the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Refined Integrity.'

sentences.zh: 後兩子學瀚、學澧皆賜舉人。

translations.literal: Later both sons Xuehan and Xueli were granted the rank of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Later both sons Xuehan and Xueli were granted the rank of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 孫銘恩，字蘭檢，江蘇通州人。

translations.literal: Sun Mingen, style name Lanjian, was a native of Tongzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mingen, whose style was Lanjian, came from Tongzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was repeatedly promoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose to mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，典試廣東，還京，道出九江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he served as examiner for Guangdong, returned to the capital, and his route passed through Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he served as Guangdong examination commissioner and returned to the capital by way of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 粵匪已由岳州東下，陷漢陽。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebels had already from Yuezhou moved east and seized Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already swept east from Yuezhou and taken Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 銘恩疏上江防十二事，下江南督撫施行。

translations.literal: Mingen memorialized submitting twelve matters on Yangzi defense, which were sent down to the governors of Jiangnan for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Mingen memorialized twelve proposals for Yangzi defense, and they were sent to the Jiangnan governors for implementation.

sentences.zh: 三年，連擢內閣學士、兵部侍郎，督安徽學政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted in succession to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of War, and supervised education in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted in turn to grand secretary and vice minister of war, and became Anhui education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時安慶已為賊踞，故事，學政駐太平府，銘恩激勵紳民，舉行團練，捐廉為倡。

translations.literal: At the time Anqing was already held by rebels; by precedent the education commissioner was stationed at Taiping Prefecture; Mingen encouraged gentry and common people, organized militia, and donated from his official salary to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing was already in rebel hands. By precedent the education commissioner was stationed at Taiping Prefecture. Mingen rallied gentry and commoners, organized militia, and gave his salary to lead by example.

sentences.zh: 潰兵時至，侮官劫市，銘恩諭以大義，稍定。

translations.literal: Routed troops arrived from time to time, insulting officials and plundering the markets; Mingen instructed them in the greater principle, and matters settled somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Routed soldiers kept arriving, insulting officials and looting the markets. Mingen appealed to their duty, and order returned somewhat.

sentences.zh: 四年，以父病請開缺省視，會有旨命偕在籍前南河總督潘錫恩防守徽、寧，銘恩未之知也。
