translations.literal: In the fourth year, because his father was ill he requested to vacate his post and return home to visit; at the same time an edict ordered him together with the retired former Governor-General of the South River Pan Xien to defend Huizhou and Ningguo, which Mingen did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked leave to visit his ill father. At the same time an edict ordered him to work with the retired former South River governor-general Pan Xien on defending Huizhou and Ningguo, which he did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 疏入，文宗疑其規避，嚴旨切責，允其回籍，俟假滿以三四品京堂降補。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Emperor Wenzong suspected he was evading duty and issued a stern edict sharply rebuking him, but allowed him to return home and ordered that after leave ended he might be demoted and appointed as third- or fourth-rank Beijing official.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Wenzong suspected evasion and rebuked him sharply, but allowed him to go home and ordered that after leave he be demoted to a third- or fourth-rank Beijing post.

sentences.zh: 未踰月，賊犯太平，從者請避之。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed the rebels attacked Taiping, and his attendants asked him to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the rebels attacked Taiping, and his attendants urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 銘恩曰：「城亡與亡，以明吾心！

translations.literal: Mingen said: 'When the city perishes, I perish with it, to show my heart!'
translations.idiomatic: Mingen said, 'When the city falls, I fall with it. That will show where I stand!'

sentences.zh: 」城陷，賊至，衣冠坐堂上，抗罵，被執，囚於江寧，僕范源從。

translations.literal: When the city fell the rebels arrived; in cap and gown he sat in the hall, resisted and reviled them, was seized, imprisoned at Jiangning, and his servant Fan Yuan followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the rebels came. Dressed in his official robes he sat in the hall, cursed them, and was seized and imprisoned at Jiangning. His servant Fan Yuan went with him.

sentences.zh: 銘恩不食，賊脅源勸降，源叱之，斷其舌，同遇害。

translations.literal: Mingen refused food; the rebels coerced Yuan to urge surrender; Yuan rebuked them, they cut out his tongue, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingen refused to eat. The rebels forced Yuan to urge him to surrender. Yuan cursed them, they cut out his tongue, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其抗節不屈，遇害甚慘，贈內閣學士，入祀京師及安徽、江蘇昭忠祠，予騎都尉世職，諡文節。

translations.literal: An edict praised his unyielding integrity, noted that his killing was very cruel, posthumously made him Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, enshrined him in the Capital and in the Shrines of Loyal Martyrs of Anhui and Jiangsu, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his unyielding integrity and the cruelty of his death, granted him posthumous rank as grand secretary, enshrined him in the capital and in the loyal-martyr shrines of Anhui and Jiangsu, gave his family the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and bestowed the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 范源同議卹。

translations.literal: Fan Yuan received condolence on the same terms.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuan received the same condolence honors.

sentences.zh: 沈炳垣，字紫卿，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Shen Bingyuan, style name Ziqing, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bingyuan, whose style was Ziqing, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, became a compiler, and was made sub-reader.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，督廣西學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he supervised education in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he became Guangxi education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣西自洪秀全北犯後，群匪迭起。

translations.literal: Since Hong Xiuquan marched north from Guangxi, bandit groups had risen one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong Xiuquan marched north from Guangxi, rebel bands rose one after another.

sentences.zh: 炳垣至，與巡撫勞崇光議戰守策，崇光深器之。

translations.literal: When Bingyuan arrived he deliberated with Governor Lao Chongguang on strategies of war and defense, and Chongguang greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingyuan arrived he worked with Governor Lao Chongguang on strategy, and Chongguang held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 七年春，按試南寧畢，警報日至，居民洶洶驚避。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, when the examinations at Nanning were finished, alarms arrived daily and the residents were greatly alarmed and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year, after examinations at Nanning, alarms arrived daily and the people fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 炳垣倡言城險可保，條列守禦法，捐俸濟餉，守三晝夜。

translations.literal: Bingyuan urged that the city's strategic strength made it defensible, set forth methods of defense in detail, donated salary to aid provisions, and held for three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan argued that the city's terrain made it defensible, laid out a defense plan, gave his salary for provisions, and held the walls for three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 賊知有備，引去。

translations.literal: The rebels, knowing there was preparation, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city prepared, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 潯州陷，江路梗塞，間道至梧州。

translations.literal: Xunzhou fell, the river routes were blocked, and he went by a side path to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhou fell and the river routes were cut. He reached Wuzhou by a back road.

sentences.zh: 艇匪陳開等眾數万突來犯，炳垣率知府陳瑞枝等嬰城固守，凡三閱月，糧盡援絕。

translations.literal: The boat bandits Chen Kai and others with a host of tens of thousands suddenly came to attack; Bingyuan led Prefect Chen Ruizhi and others to bind themselves to the city in stubborn defense; in all three months passed, grain was exhausted and relief cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Boat bandits led by Chen Kai attacked with tens of thousands of men. Bingyuan joined Prefect Chen Ruizhi in a desperate defense. After three months food and relief were gone.

sentences.zh: 官吏以炳垣無守土責，遣兵衛之出，炳垣不可。

translations.literal: The officials, because Bingyuan bore no territorial defense duty, sent soldiers to escort him out, but Bingyuan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Officials said he had no territorial defense duty and sent troops to escort him out, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 八月，城陷，仰藥未死，賊擁去，厚遇之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the city fell; he took poison but did not die; the rebels seized him and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the city fell. He took poison but did not die. The rebels seized him and treated him well.

sentences.zh: 炳垣罵賊，求死不得。

translations.literal: Bingyuan reviled the rebels and could not obtain death.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan cursed the rebels and could not die.

sentences.zh: 久之，乘間為書致巡撫劉長佑，請出兵襲城，密約城內民夾擊。

translations.literal: After a long while, seizing an interval he wrote a letter to Governor Liu Changyou requesting troops to strike the city and secretly arranged with people inside the city for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he smuggled a letter to Governor Liu Changyou asking for a strike on the city and secretly arranged for residents inside to attack from within.

sentences.zh: 事泄，賊恨甚，磔而焚之。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; the rebels hated him greatly, dismembered him, and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered. The rebels hated him fiercely, dismembered him, and burned his body.

sentences.zh: 有老卒睹炳垣慘死狀，走省城首於官。

translations.literal: An old soldier who witnessed Bingyuan's cruel death ran to the provincial capital and reported first to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: An old soldier who saw his cruel death ran to the provincial capital and reported it.

sentences.zh: 贈內閣學士，諡文節，建專祠桂林。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, given the posthumous title Wenjie, and a special shrine was built at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted posthumous rank as grand secretary, given the posthumous title Wenjie, and a special shrine was built at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 張錫庚，字星白，江蘇丹徒人，大學士玉書裔孫。

translations.literal: Zhang Xigeng, style name Xingbai, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu, a descendant of Grand Secretary Yushu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xigeng, whose style was Xingbai, came from Dantu in Jiangsu and was a descendant of Grand Secretary Yushu.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年二甲一名進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he placed first in the second class of jinshi graduates, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he placed first in the second class of jinshi graduates, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，擢順天府丞，丁父憂，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, promoted to Vice Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture, entered mourning for his father, and when mourning ended resumed his original office.
translations.idiomatic: He became a censor, was promoted to vice intendant of Shuntian Prefecture, mourned his father, and after mourning resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 疏論綠營冒濫頂名及緝捕諸弊，詔下其疏於各直省，實力整頓。

translations.literal: He memorialized discussing the abuses of the Green Standard Army in falsely claiming names on the rolls and in pursuit and arrest; an edict sent his memorial to all provinces for earnest rectification.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on Green Standard abuses such as padded rolls and lax policing. An edict sent his memorial to every province for thorough reform.

sentences.zh: 又疏言殿試貢士不限字數，聽其發抒，刪去頌辭，下部議行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that palace examination candidates should not be limited in word count, should be allowed free expression, and that laudatory formulas should be removed; the Board was ordered to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that palace examination candidates not be limited in length, that they be allowed free expression, and that laudatory formulas be dropped. The Board was ordered to act.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺卿、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs and then as left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，督浙江學政，擢刑部侍郎，仍留學政任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he supervised education in Zhejiang, was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, and still retained the education commissioner's duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he became Zhejiang education commissioner, was promoted to vice minister of justice, and kept the education post.

sentences.zh: 十年，杭州陷而旋复，錫庚助城守，其子恩然率家屬自焚，錫庚以聞，予旌卹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Hangzhou fell and was soon recovered; Xigeng assisted in defending the city; his son Enran led the family to burn themselves; Xigeng reported this and they were granted commendation and condolence.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hangzhou fell and was soon retaken. Xigeng helped defend the city. His son Enran led the family in self-immolation. Xigeng reported it, and they received honors and condolence.

sentences.zh: 團練大臣王履謙劾巡撫王有齡籌餉按缺派捐，命錫庚訪按。

translations.literal: Militia Minister Wang Lvqian impeached Governor Wang Youling for raising funds by assigning contributions according to vacancies; Xigeng was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Militia Minister Wang Lvqian impeached Governor Wang Youling for assigning contributions by official vacancy. Xigeng was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 錫庚以有齡一月內更易州縣二十馀員，非政體，請予處分，從之。

translations.literal: Xigeng held that Youling within one month had changed more than twenty prefectural and county officials, which was not proper administration, and requested punishment, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xigeng found that Youling had replaced more than twenty prefectural and county officials within a month, which was improper, and asked that he be punished. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年，任滿，代者未至，杭州復被圍，錫庚同守城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year his term ended but his replacement had not arrived; Hangzhou was besieged again, and Xigeng joined in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his term ended before his replacement arrived. Hangzhou was besieged again, and Xigeng helped defend it.

sentences.zh: 城陷，或勸之去，錫庚曰：「吾大臣也，不可辱國！

translations.literal: When the city fell some urged him to leave; Xigeng said: 'I am a great minister; I cannot disgrace the state!'
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell some urged him to flee. Xigeng said, 'I am a senior minister. I cannot disgrace the state!'

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊，賊稱其忠，為具棺斂。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself; the rebels praised his loyalty and provided a coffin for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself. The rebels praised his loyalty and gave him a coffin.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書銜，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，祀浙江昭忠祠，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted ministerial rank, given the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, enshrined in Zhejiang's Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted posthumous ministerial rank, hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of Light Cavalry, enshrined in Zhejiang's Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, and given the posthumous title Wenzhen, 'Refined Constancy.'

sentences.zh: 論曰：呂賢基以忠鯁受主知，其治兵安徽也，志欲大有所為，當殘破之馀，驟無藉手，倉猝殞身，文宗惜之。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Lv Xianji because of loyal bluntness won his ruler's trust; in governing troops in Anhui his ambition was to achieve great things, but amid the ruins there was suddenly nothing to grasp, and he perished in haste; Emperor Wenzong mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Lv Xianji won the throne's trust through blunt loyalty. When he took charge of militia in Anhui he meant to accomplish much, but amid the ruins he had nothing to work with and died suddenly. Emperor Wenzong mourned him.

sentences.zh: 鄒鳴鶴久著循聲，戴熙亦負清望，張芾守江西、防皖南，雖無偉績，備歷艱難。

translations.literal: Zou Minghe long enjoyed a reputation for benevolent administration; Dai Xi also bore a reputation for purity; Zhang Fei defended Jiangxi and guarded southern Anhui; though without great achievements, all endured hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Minghe had long been known for humane rule, Dai Xi for moral stature, and Zhang Fei for defending Jiangxi and southern Anhui. None won great victories, but all endured hardship.

sentences.zh: 三人以在籍搢紳治團籌防，雖久暫不同，皆事權不屬，或以城亡與亡，或以犯難遇害。

translations.literal: The three, as gentry at home organizing militia and planning defense, though their tenures differed in length, all lacked proper authority; some died when their cities fell, others met harm while facing danger.
translations.idiomatic: All three were local gentry organizing militia and defense. Their terms differed in length, but none held full command. Some died when their cities fell; others were killed facing danger.

sentences.zh: 黃琮初因措置失宜獲咎，繼亦原之，而終不免於難。

translations.literal: Huang Cong at first was blamed for improper arrangements, was later forgiven, but in the end could not escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong was first punished for mishandling affairs, later forgiven, but in the end could not escape death.

sentences.zh: 馮培元、孫銘恩、沈炳垣、張錫庚，文學之臣，職非守土，死皆慘烈，朝廷報忠之典悉從優渥，固不以成敗論已。

translations.literal: Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, and Zhang Xigeng were literary officials whose duties were not territorial defense; all died cruel deaths, and the court's rites rewarding loyalty were all especially generous, for reward is surely not judged by success or failure alone.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Peiyuan, Sun Mingen, Shen Bingyuan, and Zhang Xigeng were literary officials without territorial defense duties. All died cruel deaths. The court honored them generously, for loyalty is not judged by success or failure alone.
